exposure: concurrent major comorbidities (severe grade-3 or -4 intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular leukomalacia, necrotizing enterocolitis, intestinal perforation)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 939 preterm infants aged <=32 weeks of gestation admitted to a single academic network of multiple neonatal intensive care units between 2012 and 2015, with 182 of these infants diagnosed with sepsis.
finding: Preexisting comorbidities commonly associated with extreme preterm birth, such as severe intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular leukomalacia, necrotizing enterocolitis, and intestinal perforation, were found to contribute to sepsis-related mortality in preterm infants.
